sections.overview: This large skate inhabits the northeastern Pacific from the Bering Sea to Baja California. Some current taxonomic sources use the combination Beringraja binoculata.
sections.identification: It has a diamond-shaped body, mottled brown upper surface and large eye-like spots on the pectoral fins.
sections.habitat: It lives on sandy or muddy bottoms, including coastal bays and estuaries, and ranges across the continental shelf.
sections.diet: It feeds on crustaceans and fishes, as well as other marine invertebrates.
sections.behavior: It is a bottom-dwelling species and may occur over sand, mud or rocky areas.
sections.reproduction: Females lay large leathery egg cases, which can contain several embryos; young hatch after about nine months.
sections.ecology: It is one of the largest skates in North American waters and is caught in commercial fisheries.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern from 2024.
